rationale: The construction is internally consistent and the sign direction is correct, but it is essentially an additive blend of two well-known anomalies (Titman-Wei-Xie abnormal capital investment and cash-flow profitability), so any measured slope may be carried by the cash-coverage leg rather than the claimed funding-gap interaction.

This is a one-input substitution (ib for oancf) inside the archived Equity Proceeds Absorption Gap, i.e., a cosmetic variant, and the resulting expression also embeds a sign conflict (low capex raises the signal, predicting low returns, contrary to the investment anomaly it otherwise leans on) while largely re-expressing the known net-equity-issuance and profitability effects.

Direction and hypothesis are consistent, but the change in aqc/(aqc+capx) is a highly unstable ratio (undefined or jumping between 0 and 1 for firms with sporadic deals), and the second leg is plain three-year ROA, so the signal risks being a noisy overlay on the profitability anomaly.

This is a three-period smoothing of the archived Liquidity-Supported Maintenance Alignment with an identical gate and identical mechanism — a cosmetic robustness tweak rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

The slope-versus-alpha diagnosis is legitimate and the sign logic holds, but this is the third proposal in the batch applying the same "minus standardized oancf/lct" template, and the archive shows that leg alone (Inventory-Cash Coverage Imbalance) already delivers most of the alpha, so attribution to the intangible-conversion channel will be weak.

The hiring-rate anomaly is published (Belo-Lin-Bazdresch), but conditioning it on subsequent cash-coverage deterioration is a genuinely new and internally consistent MIN-gate that differs from the archive's profit-based hiring conditions, though the closely analogous capex version in the archive performed poorly, tempering expectations.
